forces.title: Subdued EU construction growth dampens capital goods demand
forces.description: Europe's construction sector is expected to experience only marginal growth of 0.5% in 2026, following a decline in 2024. This subdued activity in both residential and non-residential building, primarily due to higher interest rates and construction costs, acts as a significant headwind. It reduces overall demand for general-purpose industrial machinery, construction equipment (IN030201), and a wide array of electrical components, cables, and parts (IN030203) essential for building projects across the EU.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising input costs and energy prices for manufacturing
forces.description: Higher energy prices are significantly pushing up production costs for energy-intensive materials like concrete, cement, and bricks, which are inputs for construction, and also impacting manufacturers within IG0302. While input prices are rising gradually, passing these costs through the value chain is becoming harder due to higher interest rates for customers. This cost accumulation puts pressure on profit margins for manufacturers of industrial machinery and electrical components, potentially affecting investment and profitability.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Increased infrastructure and energy network investments
forces.description: Infrastructure investment, supported by EU funds and spending on energy and digital networks, is a positive offset to weak building sectors. The EU energy construction sector has been growing since 2022, driven by investments in renewable energy sources, grid upgrades, and energy efficiency. This sustained investment provides a significant tailwind for manufacturers of Heavy Electrical Equipment (IN030202) like power turbines and large transformers, as well as Electrical Components, Cables & Parts (IN030203) and construction equipment (IN030201).
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Slowing Dutch infrastructure growth due to cost and budget limits
forces.description: While the Dutch infrastructure sector has shown high growth, its growth rate is slowing in 2026 and 2027. This deceleration is attributed to high construction costs, persistent staff shortages, nitrogen restrictions, and limited government budgets prioritizing maintenance over new construction. This acts as a headwind for manufacturers of construction equipment (IN030201), heavy electrical equipment (IN030202), and electrical components (IN030203) by reducing the momentum of new project demand, though maintenance-related demand may stabilize.
forces.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

forces.title: Data centre buildout drives demand for electrical equipment
forces.description: The increasing buildout of data centres in Norway is significantly boosting demand for various capital goods. This directly benefits manufacturers of Heavy Electrical Equipment (IN030202) and Electrical Components, Cables & Parts (IN030203), as it increases demand for essential components such as cables, transformers, switchboards, and other energy supply equipment. This trend contributes to accelerating investment growth across sectors, indicating a strong positive impact on the production and sales of these capital goods.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Increased defense spending boosts manufacturing activity
forces.description: Continued increases in spending on defense, security, and preparedness are providing a significant tailwind for manufacturers in Norway, affecting both domestic and export markets. This drives demand for specialized industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201) used in defense systems and platforms. The sustained investment ensures a pipeline of orders and production activity for companies involved in this strategic sector, contributing to overall growth in Capital Goods & Machinery.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Strong international competition from Asian manufacturers
forces.description: Norwegian manufacturers, particularly those involved in producing energy supply equipment like cables, transformers, and switchboards (IN030202, IN030203), are facing strong international competition, especially from Asian manufacturers. This competitive pressure dampens activity and expectations, making it challenging for domestic firms to maintain market share and pricing power. It represents a significant headwind that could affect profitability and investment decisions within these segments of the Capital Goods & Machinery sector.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Food & Beverage sector investing in automation and robotics
forces.description: Food and beverage producers in Ireland are increasing investments in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods to boost productivity, counter labor shortages, and manage costs. This trend serves as a direct tailwind for the Industrial Machinery & Equipment sector (IN030201), particularly those manufacturing food processing machinery, industrial automation systems, and robots. This sustained demand from a critical customer sector offers significant growth opportunities for capital goods providers specializing in efficiency-enhancing technologies.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Cost and trade pressures on Irish machinery SMEs
forces.description: SMEs within Ireland's specialized machinery & equipment sector (IN030201), particularly in engineering and material handling, face exposure to increasing labor costs, liquidity constraints, and general cost pressures. Additionally, international trade uncertainty, including potential tariff exposure, creates market volatility and risk of margin erosion. These factors act as significant headwinds, requiring firms to prioritize strong cash discipline and careful review of pricing strategies and hedging arrangements to maintain profitability and investment capacity.

forces.title: Cheap Chinese imports pressure European machinery markets
forces.description: Major European markets, including chemicals, steel, cars, and machinery, are experiencing significant pressure from the rapid rise in cheap imports from China. This is compounded by low labor costs, technological advancements, subsidies, and currency valuation in China. This influx of low-cost goods creates a substantial headwind for European manufacturers of industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201) and heavy electrical equipment/components (IN030202, IN030203), leading to increased competition and pressure on pricing and profitability.
forces.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

forces.title: Electrification and defense spending benefit manufacturing
forces.description: Parts of the Dutch metals, machinery, and electrotechnical industries are benefiting from strong tailwinds driven by electrification trends and increased defense spending. Electrification fuels demand for electrical components, motors, and related manufacturing equipment (IN030201, IN030202, IN030203), while defense spending boosts specialized machinery production (IN030201). These strategic shifts provide significant growth opportunities, offsetting pressures in other industrial segments and supporting sustained activity and investment in these areas.
forces.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

forces.title: Belgium's residential construction downturn limits new orders
forces.description: Belgium's residential construction sector continues to weaken, with building permits declining in 2025. This sustained downturn, particularly in apartment projects, is creating a supply-demand mismatch for smaller housing units. The slow recovery and projected slight upward trend in interest rates make a strong rebound unlikely in the near term. This acts as a significant headwind for manufacturers of construction equipment (IN030201) and electrical components (IN030203) tied to new residential builds.
forces.source_title: Belgium’s housing supply–demand mismatch widened further in 2025

forces.title: Strategic investment in automation and AI drives demand
forces.description: Despite global volatility, businesses are recognizing the competitive advantage of strategic investments in sustainability, automation, and AI. This pragmatic approach leads to a focus on leveraging these opportunities, driving demand for industrial automation, robotics (IN030201), and related electrical components. Businesses are prioritizing investments that enhance productivity and future-proof operations, creating a significant upside for Capital Goods & Machinery providers that offer advanced, efficient, and sustainable solutions for various industrial applications.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Maritime green transition fuels demand for eco-friendly vessel equipment
forces.description: The Norwegian maritime industry's commitment to a green transition, targeting climate neutrality by 2050, is generating substantial demand for new, low- and zero-emission vessel technology. Shipping companies are investing heavily in innovative solutions for emission reduction. This provides a strong tailwind for manufacturers of specialized industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201) and electrical components, cables & parts (IN030203) that are critical for developing and equipping climate-neutral ships and offshore wind installations, fostering innovation and new order intake.

forces.title: Reduced petroleum tax projects dampen oil services activity
forces.description: The completion of numerous projects initiated in response to the petroleum tax package is leading to a dampening of activity on the Norwegian continental shelf. This directly impacts the oil services sector, which is a key customer for specialized industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201). The reduction in new field developments means lower demand for new capital goods, creating a headwind for manufacturers supplying this segment, despite some ongoing activity in operations and maintenance.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Europe's construction sector faces weak growth, dampening capital goods demand
viewpoints.description: Europe's construction sector is expected to experience subdued growth, with EU output projected to grow by a marginal 0.5% in 2026. This weak growth, driven by higher financing costs and geopolitical risks, will likely cap momentum for industrial machinery, equipment, and electrical components, particularly those tied to residential and non-residential building activities, which remain weak spots in the broader economy. This suggests a cautious outlook for related capital goods manufacturers.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: EU energy construction sector growing strongly, boosting electrical equipment demand
viewpoints.description: The EU energy construction sector is demonstrating robust growth, a trend observed since 2022. This expansion is primarily fuelled by significant investments in renewable energy sources, grid infrastructure upgrades, and various energy efficiency projects across the region. This sustained growth provides a positive outlook and serves as a strong tailwind for manufacturers of Heavy Electrical Equipment (e.g., power turbines, HVDC systems) and Electrical Components, Cables & Parts, as demand for these products is directly linked to energy infrastructure development.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Dutch infrastructure growth strong but slowing, impacting machinery demand
viewpoints.description: The Dutch infrastructure sector has shown persistently high growth rates since 2020, with a significant 10.5% volume growth in 2025. This strong performance provides substantial demand for industrial machinery, heavy electrical equipment, and electrical components. However, growth is projected to slow in 2026 and 2027 due to factors such as high construction costs, staff shortages, and limited government budgets prioritizing maintenance over new construction. This indicates a continued but decelerating positive demand for capital goods.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Norwegian manufacturing boosted by data centers and defense spending
viewpoints.description: Norwegian manufacturing is experiencing an uplift in activity driven by increased data center buildout and higher defense spending. The data center expansion specifically fuels demand for cables, transformers, switchboards, and other energy supply equipment (IN030202, IN030203). Additionally, continued investment in defense and security boosts activity for specialized industrial machinery and equipment manufacturers (IN030201). This creates a positive outlook for these segments within the Capital Goods & Machinery sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish Food & Beverage sector increasing automation, driving machinery demand
viewpoints.description: The Irish Food and Beverage industry is increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods. This strategic shift is aimed at improving productivity, mitigating labor shortages, and effectively managing escalating costs. This trend presents a strong positive outlook for the Industrial Machinery & Equipment sector (IN030201), as food processing machinery and industrial automation solutions are in high demand to support these operational efficiency initiatives within the food and beverage industry.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Construction sector strengthens, especially civil engineering activity
viewpoints.description: Ireland's construction sector is showing sustained strengthening, with growth now broad-based across segments. Notably, civil engineering activity is at its highest level since 2022, providing a robust tailwind for manufacturers of construction equipment (IN030201) and associated electrical components and parts (IN030203). While housing remains the weakest segment, the overall recovery, particularly in commercial and civil engineering projects, signals a positive demand environment for industrial machinery and equipment, supporting the sector's performance.

viewpoints.title: Ireland's specialized machinery sector shows stable fundamentals amidst pressures
viewpoints.description: Ireland's machinery & equipment sector maintains a specialized and export-focused profile, particularly in engineering and material handling, with stable fundamentals supporting growth. However, SMEs within this sector are exposed to rising labor, liquidity, and input cost pressures. International trade uncertainty also contributes to market volatility. Despite these headwinds, the sector's focus on innovation and quality, serving key industries like logistics, construction, and agrifood, suggests a resilient yet cautiously positive outlook, requiring strong financial discipline to navigate challenges.

viewpoints.title: Greek Food & Beverage industry pursues digital transformation, boosting automation
viewpoints.description: The Greek Food and Beverage industry is undergoing an intense digital transformation, adopting automation, data analytics, and smart manufacturing. This shift is influencing production, distribution, and R&D, creating new operational models to address challenges such as rising energy costs and inflationary pressures. This strategic move by a key customer sector provides a positive impetus for manufacturers of industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201), particularly those specializing in automation and integrated production solutions, as they are crucial enablers of this transformation.
viewpoints.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

viewpoints.title: Dutch machinery sector mixed: electrification and defense positive, trucks pressured
viewpoints.description: The Dutch metals, machinery, and electrotechnical industries present a mixed outlook. They are benefiting significantly from electrification trends and increased defense spending, providing tailwinds for relevant capital goods (IN030201, IN030202, IN030203). However, other segments, particularly truck manufacturing (IN030201) and energy-intensive basic industries, remain under pressure from factors such as cheap imports from China and high energy costs. This dichotomy suggests that while certain areas will thrive, others face considerable headwinds, resulting in a neutral to cautious outlook overall.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

viewpoints.title: Norwegian construction growth dampens, offset by energy and defense investment
viewpoints.description: Norway's construction sector faces continued dampening growth due to low new-build activity and higher building costs, indicating a cautious outlook for related industrial machinery and electrical components. However, this is partly offset by positive contributions from energy supply development, data center buildout, and increased defense investment. These areas drive demand for specialized equipment (IN030201), heavy electrical equipment (IN030202), and electrical components (IN030203), providing some counterbalance to the broader construction slowdown and leading to a mixed, but slightly negative, outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

viewpoints.title: Norwegian maritime green transition drives demand for new vessel technology
viewpoints.description: The Norwegian maritime industry is actively undergoing a green transition, with shipping companies investing heavily in new technologies and solutions to reduce emissions and achieve climate neutrality by 2050. This focus on equipping vessels with climate-neutral technology, including Norwegian-developed solutions, presents a significant positive outlook for manufacturers of specialized industrial machinery and equipment (IN030201) and advanced electrical components and parts (IN030203). The demand for low and zero-emission maritime technology creates substantial new opportunities for these capital goods providers.

demand_drivers.description: Supported by EU funds and spending on energy and digital networks, infrastructure investment provides an offset to weak building sector, driving demand for heavy electrical equipment, cables, and construction machinery.

Expected growth in Germany's construction sector in 2026, after five years of contraction, will gradually gain momentum into 2027, supported by housing and infrastructure, boosting demand for related capital goods.

market_sizing.methodology: The EU construction sector output is forecast to grow by a marginal 0.5% in 2026, following a 1.8% decline in 2024 and 2.3% growth in 2025. This indicates the overall market demand trend for construction equipment (IN030201) and electrical components/parts (IN030203) used in construction. The building sector remains weak due to higher interest rates and costs, while infrastructure investment is an offsetting driver.
